name: /poteto-mode
obligation: The /poteto-mode command must enable sticky mode and match the playbook for the given task.

name: /poteto-mode-off
obligation: The /poteto-mode-off command must disable sticky mode and notify the user.
The playbook matcher must score rules by priority and cue presence, requiring a minimum score of 2.
The sticky input hook must only evaluate input events originating from interactive, rpc, or unknown provenance.
The sticky input hook must transform qualifying user text into a /skill:poteto-mode invocation to force sticky routing.
verification: test@tests/layers/01-unit/sticky-session.test.ts@prefixes the playbook path and keeps an existing invocation

obligation: The before_agent_start handler must append the skill body capped at 48000 bytes and the playbook body capped at 24000 bytes.
The poteto runtime must restore sticky state from the latest pstack-poteto-mode custom entry upon session_start.
The sticky input hook must bypass playbook matching and force-invocation entirely when PSTACK_CHILD_ROLE is set.
The sticky input hook must automatically arm readonly mode for an investigation playbook match if the text is short and score is high.
The sticky input hook must not reassign the matched playbook on a casual turn, and the sticky prompt must inject the assigned playbook instead of re-matching the turn text.
The playbook matcher must require context beyond the bare word bugbot to route to the Babysit playbook.
verification: test@tests/layers/01-unit/runtime-wiring.test.ts@matches by cue and by explicit playbook path

obligation: The before_agent_start handler must inject the sticky prompt on every turn while poteto mode is armed.
verification: test@tests/layers/01-unit/runtime-wiring.test.ts@poteto prompt handler adds the sticky body when armed

name: /pstack-readonly
obligation: The /pstack-readonly command must arm readonly mode with a command reason.

name: /pstack-readonly-off
obligation: The /pstack-readonly-off command must disable readonly mode and restore original tools.
Arming readonly mode must strip write, edit, bash, and powershell tools from the active set while preserving others.
Disabling readonly mode must restore the exact tool set that was active before arming.
The readonly tool_call policy must block the pstack_loop arm path (subprocess watcher) while allowing status, list, and stop.
verification: test@tests/layers/01-unit/readonly-state.test.ts@readonly policy blocks exec, writers, fan-out, and frame mutations

obligation: The readonly tool_call policy must block pstack_decision_log and pstack_benny_wake writes while allowing pstack_benny_wake path.
verification: test@tests/layers/01-unit/readonly-state.test.ts@readonly policy blocks exec, writers, fan-out, and frame mutations

obligation: The readonly tool_call policy must block mutating worktree, ship, babysit, and deslop tool calls while coercing pstack_spawn to readonly.
Arming readonly mode must display a pstack-ro status indicator in the UI.
The readonly state must be persisted across session_start events using the pstack-session-readonly custom entry.
An explicit investigation skill invocation or a high-scoring playbook match must auto-arm readonly mode.
The readonly policy must block pstack_swarm and pstack_arena so a readonly session cannot fan out write-capable children.
verification: test@tests/layers/01-unit/readonly-state.test.ts@readonly policy blocks exec, writers, fan-out, and frame mutations

obligation: The readonly policy must block the pstack_control_cli exec channel so a readonly session runs no subprocesses.
verification: test@tests/layers/01-unit/readonly-state.test.ts@readonly policy blocks exec, writers, fan-out, and frame mutations

obligation: The readonly keep-set must preserve the READONLY_TOOLS read allowlist when the tool registry reports a narrower set.
verification: test@tests/layers/01-unit/readonly-state.test.ts@preserves the read allowlist when the registry narrows

obligation: A strong non-investigation playbook match must release a readonly session that the sticky matcher armed.
